title: The Significance of Steadfastness (Istiqamah)
summary: Istiqamah means steadfast adherence to God's path in all aspects of life.
translation: What is steadfastness, i.e., Istiqamah? The word 'Istiqamah' is small, but its meaning holds a grand vastness. In a literal sense, it means to stand upright without leaning to any side. However, in the context of Shariah and Sunnah, it implies that a person remains straight on Allah’s path in their beliefs, dealings, acts of worship, character, social life, earning, spending, and all areas of life, adhering to the boundaries set by Allah without deviating in any aspect. It is not about performing an action against Shariah when something contrary appears but rather adhering completely to the commands of Shariah and practicing it consistently. Hence, it is narrated about the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that no verse was revealed to him more difficult during his prophethood than the verse from Surah Hud: 'So remain on a right course as you have been commanded' (11:112). At one occasion, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Surah Hud made me old.' It refers specifically to this verse. If any advice is paramount, it is maintaining steadfastness in faith and practice until death. A companion named Sufyan Thaqafi, perhaps Sufyan bin Abdullah Thaqafi, requested a comprehensive piece of advice, upon which the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Say I have believed in Allah, then remain steadfast.' Thus, steadfastness means remaining firm, not swept away by inclinations, but maintaining faith in Allah and His Messenger. Promises of great rewards are mentioned for those who declare, 'Our Lord is Allah' and maintain this course: angels will descend upon them, saying, 'Do not fear or grieve but rejoice in Paradise that you are promised.' On this life and the Hereafter, they will be friends, and they will receive whatever they desire and ask for, enjoying the hospitality of Allah, Who is Forgiving, Merciful. This Qur’anic verse from Surah Hamim Sajda highlights the significant promises for steadfastness, showing its great importance as divine advice and urging consistent adherence to it throughout one’s life.
